in_hebrew.name: פטריאל
in_hebrew.long_meaning: פטריאל הוא שם שמשמעותו 'אלוהים הוא אבי' או 'אבי האלוהים'. השם מורכב מהמילים 'פטר' שפירושו אב ואל שפירושו אלוהים. השם פטריאל קשור קשר הדוק לאמונה באלוהים כסמכות עליונה וביטוי של כניעה לרצונו.

in_greek.name: Πατριήλ
in_greek.long_meaning: Το όνομα Πατριήλ προέρχεται από τις λέξεις 'πατήρ' που σημαίνει πατέρας και 'Θεός' που σημαίνει Θεός. Στη Βίβλο, ο Θεός αναφέρεται συχνά ως ο Πατέρας, υπογραμμίζοντας τη σχέση αγάπης και φροντίδας μεταξύ του Θεού και των πιστών. Το όνομα Πατριήλ αντανακλά την πνευματική σχέση του ανθρώπου με τον Θεό.

in_latin.name: Patriel
in_latin.long_meaning: Nomen Patriel derivatur ex vocibus 'pater' et 'Deus'. In traditione christiana, Deus saepe ut Pater refertur, qui relationem amoris et providentiae inter Deum et fideles significat. Nomen Patriel pietatem et devotionem ad Deum patrem exprimit.

in_english.name: Patriel
in_english.long_meaning: The name Patriel is derived from Hebrew roots, meaning 'God is my father' or 'Father of God'. It signifies a deep spiritual connection with God as a paternal figure, embodying trust, love, and obedience. Historically, the concept of God as Father is central to Christian theology, reflecting God's nurturing and protective love for humanity. The name Patriel is chosen for its strong biblical connotations and its expression of faith in God.

data.cultural_impact: The name Patriel carries a rich cultural heritage as it represents the ancient Hebrew tradition that places a high value on the role of the father and the family in society. Patriel signifies strength, loyalty, and the sustaining power of the familial bond.
data.spiritual_significance: Spiritually, Patriel is a reminder of our connection to our Heavenly Father. It is a dignified name that conveys a deep sense of reverence and respect for the Creator and the nurturing, loving role that He plays as a Father to His people. The name Patriel encourages a heartfelt relationship with God as we seek to emulate the devoted, loving, and caring attributes of our heavenly Father.

historical_references.reference: Patriel of Babylon was a deacon who was martyred during the reign of Emperor Decius (AD 249-251), along with the bishop Proterius and 14 other Christians in the city of Babylon. The Roman authorities had issued a decree that all citizens must offer sacrifices to the gods, and those who refused would be put to death. Patriel and the others adhered to their faith and refused to comply, and were martyred for their refusal.
historical_references.context: Emperor Decius and Roman persecution of Christians

historical_references.reference: Patriel of Jerusalem, also known as Patroclus or Patrokles, was a deacon who lived in the late 4th or early 5th century. He is best known for his association with St. Jerome and his translation of the Bible from the original Hebrew and Greek into Latin. Patriel is believed to have been a disciple of Jerome and assisted him in his work on the translation, which became known as the Vulgate.
historical_references.context: St. Jerome and the translation of the Bible into Latin

modern_usage.modern_context: The name Patriel, derived from the biblical character Patricius (or Patricks), is not a commonly used name in modern times. However, it may be seen in certain contexts, such as modern Hebrew literature, where authors may choose to use biblical names for their characters. In Israeli names, Patriel may appear as a variant of the more common name Patrik or Patryk. In the field of biblical studies, scholars may use this name in their research or publications related to the study of Patricius and his significance in Christianity and the Bible.
